kicker: A browser for agents, from source

steps.say: This is a web browser running entirely inside Cloudflare Workers. No Chrome, no container.

steps.caption: Pages rendered by Kitesurf, DevTools attached over CDP
steps.say: It is called Kitesurf. Cloudflare built it for agents, and this week it went open source.

scenes.headline: How a browser fits inside Workers isolates
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Skerry! I read Kitesurf's code to see which parts of a browser it kept, and what one page really costs.

stations.label: Fetch
stations.sub: the only way out to the internet

stations.label: Style and layout
stations.sub: Servo's CSS engine, then the scene

stations.label: Encode
stations.sub: Krilla writes the PDF as vectors

steps.say: A browser does the same work in the same order. First it fetches. In Kitesurf one gateway Worker does every fetch.

steps.term: Dynamic Worker: an isolate created at runtime
steps.say: Then it parses HTML into a DOM, here Rust compiled to WebAssembly, in a fresh isolate for every page.
Then the page's own JavaScript runs. Hold that thought.
Then style and layout, with Servo's CSS engine. The page isolate also records the scene to draw.
For a screenshot, a second isolate replays that scene into pixels on the CPU. Real pixels, no GPU. For plain text, it never starts.
Last, it encodes a PNG or JPEG, or writes a vector PDF.

steps.caption: Bake the scripts, then load a fresh isolate
steps.say: Cloudflare's own diagram. The engine is the only part that keeps state, and only for one WebSocket session.
Every frame is a call to the renderer, which pulls the scene and sends back JPEG bytes. It holds nothing, so it can be killed and reloaded any time.

params.next: Next page, same session: the learned chunk is baked too

steps.say: Workers forbid eval, so a browser cannot just hand page code to V8 at runtime. Kitesurf splits the scripts in two.
Scripts it finds in the HTML, it fetches and bakes into the code the page's Dynamic Worker is created from. V8 runs those natively.
A script the page inserts later cannot be baked in time. It runs on Boa, a JavaScript interpreter compiled to WebAssembly.

steps.term: Boa: a JavaScript engine written in Rust
steps.say: So does anything an agent sends over CDP. Every page dot evaluate from Puppeteer runs on the interpreter.
On the next page of the same session, the chunks it learned are baked too, and V8 takes over.
Because the renderer only reads a scene, it can live somewhere else.

steps.caption: The page runs on Workers, the terminal draws it
steps.say: Here it runs in a terminal. The page still executes on Cloudflare.

states.say: To work with Puppeteer and Playwright, it speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol. The version it pins has fifty-eight domains.

states.term: CDP: the protocol Puppeteer speaks to Chrome
states.say: Fifteen are routed, with a hundred and eleven methods handled. Thirty answer every call with an empty success. Thirteen say not found.

steps.say: For most agent work that is enough. Here an agent lists a page's WebMCP tools through it.
But the empty success is the trap. A script that sets a time zone is told it worked.

scenes.title: Memory for one screenshot, median page
scenes.note: Cloudflare's harness, 38 pages, run of 13 November
scenes.say: Cloudflare's benchmark says the design pays off in memory and CPU on the median page. It loses on wall time, and heavy news pages flip the CPU win.

scenes.title: What a self-hosted screenshot is billed

parts.note: at least two: the page and the renderer
parts.say: But nobody bills that memory. Host it yourself and each screenshot loads at least two Dynamic Workers.
The price list charges for every one created.
So the creation fee is the bill. At ten thousand screenshots a day, about twelve hundred dollars a month.

steps.say: And yes, it runs Doom.

scenes.text: A real browser built from isolates: cheap for Cloudflare to run, free in beta, not yet cheap to host.
scenes.say: Kitesurf is a real browser built from isolates. Cheap for Cloudflare to run, free in beta, and not yet cheap to host yourself.

recap: Baked scripts on V8, everything else on Boa
111 CDP methods handled, unknown ones succeed silently
Self-hosted, the Dynamic Worker fee is the bill
scenes.say: Baked scripts on V8, the rest on Boa. A partial protocol. And a bill set by isolates. Thanks for watching!
